transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I guess what brings me in is this constant restless feeling. It’s like I’m wound too tight all the time, and I can’t really settle, even when nothing is actually happening or I’m supposed to be calm.

Like, if I’m sitting in a planning meeting at work, I can feel myself wanting to move or do something, and it’s not just boredom exactly—it’s this internal motor sort of feeling. And it even happens during things that are supposed to be relaxing for me, like painting or yoga. I’ll be there trying to be present and calm, and instead I feel like I’m fighting this urge to get up or shift around or like I can’t fully land in my own body, if that makes sense.

It’s been frustrating because I feel like I should be able to just sit and relax, especially during things I chose to do to unwind, but I don’t. I feel wound up.
Did this restless feeling start after you began or changed any medication?

I don’t think so… at least, I haven’t connected it to anything like that. I mean, I’d have to think through the timing more carefully, because I’m not always great at remembering exactly when something started versus when I changed something, but nothing jumps out to me as, “Oh, this started right after a medication change.”

It feels more like something I’ve just been dealing with, not like a sudden reaction to a new pill or anything. But if you mean even small changes or over-the-counter stuff, I’m not totally sure how detailed you want me to get.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things?

I don’t know that I’d describe it as worrying about lots of different things, exactly. I mean, I do think about things, of course—work stuff, errands, whether I forgot to respond to someone, that kind of normal life noise—but I’m not sure it’s “worry” in the sense of sitting there imagining disasters or going over and over problems.

It’s more like my mind and body don’t settle, if that makes sense. But if you’re asking whether I’m constantly anxious about a bunch of areas of my life, I don’t think that’s really the main thing I notice. I’d probably need examples of what you mean, because I might be interpreting “worry” too narrowly.
Have there been times when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

I’m not sure I’ve had that, no. I mean, there are nights where I don’t sleep well, or I get less sleep than I should, and then I sort of push through the next day because I have to, but I wouldn’t say I feel great or unusually energized from it.

If anything, I usually notice I’m tired or more scattered when I haven’t slept enough. I don’t think I’ve had a stretch where I only needed a few hours and felt totally fine or full of energy, like it didn’t affect me. At least nothing that stands out in that way.
Since you were a child, have you often had trouble paying attention or staying organized?

Yes, I think so—though the thing I remember most clearly from when I was little was less like, “She can’t pay attention quietly,” and more that I was always kind of bursting out of the chair, if that makes sense.

In elementary school, I remember getting notes sent home because I kept popping out of my seat, talking over other kids, and blurting out answers before the teacher had even finished asking the question. I can still picture that feeling of knowing I was supposed to wait, but the answer or comment was just right there and I’d already said it before I really thought it through. So yes, school organization and paying attention were part of it, but the examples that stand out are those classroom notes about me interrupting and not staying seated.
Do these restless feelings ever come in sudden attacks with a wave of intense fear or panic?

Not really, no. I mean, I get restless—like I feel wound up or like I need to move or do something—but I don’t think it comes on like an “attack,” if that makes sense.

I don’t usually have this sudden wave where I’m terrified or panicking out of nowhere. It’s more of a constant internal motor feeling than a big surge of fear. If I’m rushing or overstimulated I might feel keyed up, but I wouldn’t describe it as intense fear or panic. At least, not that I’ve noticed.
Has this restless, hard-to-sit-still feeling been present most of your life?

Yes, I think it really has. When I think back, it wasn’t just something that started in adulthood or with work stress or anything like that. I can remember being like this even in elementary school.

I used to get notes sent home because I kept popping up out of my seat when I was supposed to stay put, or I’d be talking over classmates, or I’d rush to answer before the teacher had even finished asking the question. It’s almost embarrassing remembering it, because it wasn’t like I was trying to be rude—I just felt like I had to say it or move right then. So yes, that hard-to-sit-still feeling has been there for as long as I can remember.
